A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACTIONREASONINGBENCH. Their text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions to benchmark coverage and experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLM evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, human assessments and diagnostic analyses in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, fine-tuning results, paraphrase naturalness ratings and GPT-4o/o1-preview ramification experiments.

M1.justification: The four-stage PDDL-to-ASP-to-questions pipeline remains, but its final stage gains Llama-3.1-70B paraphrasing after template generation. Natural-language variants per object, action and fluent decrease from up to five to three. These are concrete changes to a retained generation procedure (Section 3.4 and Figure 1).

E1.justification: Coverage contracts from 13 domains to eight, dropping Goldminer, Logistics, Miconic, NPuzzle and Zenotravel. Hallucination-detection and obfuscated scenarios disappear. Object Tracking loses its separate category, although object-property queries remain within Fluent Tracking. V2 introduces deeper ramification scenarios with newly defined fluents and dependencies up to four levels.

E2.justification: V1's reported comparisons include Gemini Pro, Llama2-7B/13B, Llama3-8B and Gemma-7B alongside GPT-4o. V2 retains GPT-4o but replaces those comparators with Llama-3.1-8B/70B and adds o1-preview specifically for ramifications. The fine-tuned comparator also changes from Llama3-8B to Llama-3.1-8B.

E3.justification: Reported train/test totals change from 104,894/6,216 to 149,237/3,498. V2 centers zero-shot-CoT and three-shot evaluation instead of v1's zero-shot and multiple few-shot settings. Llama-3.1-70B replaces RoBERTa for free-answer scoring, while human evaluation focuses on ramifications. Fine-tuning changes from two epochs to six for binary and eighteen for free answers. Test lengths 1, 10 and 19 remain.

E4.justification: V2 removes obfuscation robustness comparisons, transportation/non-transportation analyses, ROUGE failure tests and the accuracy-versus-state-complexity analysis. It adds paired template/paraphrase naturalness assessment, comparisons between composite-question combinations, and concrete GPT-4o/o1-preview ramification error cases. Length, fluent, prompting and fine-tuning analyses remain but are substantially revised.

E5.justification: Both retain sample-based SEM for accuracy using the same formula, without documented repeated-run or seed practices. However, v2's domain summary in Table 12 drops the instance-level mean and standard-deviation columns reported in v1 Table 18, reducing descriptive statistical reporting.

E6.justification: The performance matrices are extensively replaced for revised coverage, models, prompts and scoring. V2 newly reports GPT-4o's 0% and o1-preview's 18.42% overall accuracy on its ramification test, and paired naturalness ratings of 4.2 versus 4.5 for templated and paraphrased questions. These are results under changed settings, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The eight retained domains' state-space expressions move from v1 Appendix G to v2 Appendix F essentially unchanged. Expressions for the five removed domains disappear, and the explicit planning-instance and nested-transition definition in v1 Appendix F.18 is shortened in v2 Appendix G. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: V1 presents a broad eight-category benchmark, including hallucination detection and obfuscation, and emphasizes general RAC difficulties. V2 reframes the contribution around six diagnostic categories, foundational versus complex questions, and deeper ramifications. Its abstract and conclusion newly foreground complete GPT-4o failure and limited o1-preview success on the revised ramification test.

C2.justification: V2 adds hypotheses connecting static-fluent errors to long-context recall, few-shot degradation to spurious correlations, and ramification failures to memorized domain knowledge. Fine-tuning is interpreted much more positively than v1's mixed findings. Beyond the retained English-only and model-resource limitations, Section 7 adds planning-domain bias, prompt sensitivity, restricted RAC complexity and imperfect evaluator limitations.

D1.justification: V2 adds full PDDL descriptions for retained domains, systematic fluent classifications, named planning tools, evaluator-prompt examples, gradient accumulation and filtered fine-tuning sample counts. Hardware changes from eight A100s to eight H100s. Conversely, most detailed task/prompt examples and v1's code/data access link disappear; this establishes lost access information, not that the resources themselves became unavailable.

R1.justification: The literature coverage is substantially refocused. V1's AutoPlanBench/data-generation connection, multimodal RAC discussion and much broader agent/reasoning literature are removed. V2 adds zero-shot-CoT, newer model and reasoning-benchmark references, prompt-format bias and long-context explanations. The central comparison with PlanBench and TRAC persists, including material previously discussed in v1's appendix.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark explanations and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Data creation and validation are combined, limitations become a main-text section, and appendices are reorganized around an introductory instance, domain specifications, fluent classifications and model responses. Fluent terminology is also regrouped, including self-derived fluents.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to include paraphrasing, and Figure 2 becomes a three-model plot combining answer formats. Numerous earlier diagnostic and training plots disappear. Result tables change model columns and category structure, naturalness ratings gain paired columns, and new training-distribution tables and consistently styled example/code boxes substantially alter presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 adds deeper ramification tests, updated model comparisons, paired fluency assessment and clearer technical documentation. However, it removes obfuscation controls and the code/data link, while replacing the free-answer evaluator without reporting the human-agreement evidence promised in Section 4 and Appendix E. Appendix C also gives validation sample counts inconsistent with eight domains. These substantive gains and unresolved losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
